  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The active root command says the later sweep “removes what it would have” and omits the instruction to exclude IDs whose deletion was denied, allowing a later sweep to retry a denied cleanup deletion.
  WHY: A session following the root command can violate CLAUDE.md §26.G and §26.I and accumulate classifier refusals toward an unattended-stage stall; reviewers disagreed on severity (MAJOR vs BLOCKER), so the highest severity is retained.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 20, line 204 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root command still says the later sweep “removes what it would have,” and its Arming-the-wait step 0 lacks the exclusion cue that the twin has.
  WHY: A session reading the root command before the tenth [claude-twin-sync] could retry a denied delete_trigger during the later sweep, violating CLAUDE.md section 26.G and section 26.I.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 20, step 2 "Context" bullet, final clause; Arming the wait step 0 (around line 204, "0. **Sweep, then the hand-back Routine.** Run the stale Routine sweep (CLAUDE.md §26.G).") | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root command retains the contradictory wording "and a later sweep (Arming the wait, step 0) removes what it would have," and its Arming the wait step 0 has no inline cue to exclude trigger IDs whose `delete_trigger` was denied earlier.
  WHY: A session following the root command can retry the denied cleanup call in the later sweep, repeating the classifier-accumulation failure mode the PR exists to prevent.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "no flow retries a denied cleanup call" (issue #5068 acceptance criterion; restated in the PR description's "Findings fixed" rationale and §26.I's body text as "in that step or a later one").
  Expected change site: `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:test_step_2_sweep_is_skipped_after_a_denied_delete` and the root command `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` lines 20 and ~204.
  Evidence of absence: The test takes only `twin_text` as a parameter and asserts (a) "removes what it would have" is not in `twin_text`, (b) the corrected wording is in `twin_text`'s step 2 context, and (c) the twin's Arming the wait step 0 carries the exclusion cue. It does NOT assert anything against `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`. The root command at line 20 still contains "a later sweep (Arming the wait, step 0) removes what it would have" and the root command's Arming the wait step 0 lacks the exclusion cue. Because the root command is what sessions actually read at runtime, the test gives false coverage: it passes while the runtime defect persists in the file sessions follow. The PR description acknowledges this is the Q40 twin-first pattern with the head on hold pending the tenth `[claude-twin-sync]`, but the test does not encode that gate (e.g., by asserting the root is byte-identical to the twin, or by skipping when the tenth sync has not landed), so the mergeable state is not enforced by CI.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: The active root command says the later arming sweep “removes what it would have,” while the template says it leaves out trigger IDs whose deletion was denied; the root’s arming step also lacks that exclusion cue.
  WHY: A stage following the root command can retry a denied cleanup deletion during the later sweep, contrary to CLAUDE.md §26.G and §26.I. The root and template files also differ, so the byte-for-byte assertion in test_template_parity fails.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: “No flow retries a denied cleanup call.”
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md, step 2 Context and Arming-the-wait step 0, kept aligned with the template twin; tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py should verify the active root copy.
  Evidence of absence: The root command still says the later sweep “removes what it would have” at line 20 and does not say to exclude denied IDs at line 204. The template has the corrected wording at both sites, but test_step_2_sweep_is_skipped_after_a_denied_delete checks only twin_text, not the root command.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 20 (step 2 Context bullet, final clause) and line 204 (Arming-the-wait step 0) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root command still says "a later sweep (Arming the wait, step 0) removes what it would have," and at line 204 has no inline cue to exclude trigger IDs whose deletion was denied earlier.
  WHY: A session reading the root command at step 2 or Arming-the-wait step 0 will interpret the later sweep as retrying the denied Routine's deletion, contrary to CLAUDE.md §26.G and §26.I, and the test validates only the twin.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "no flow retries a denied cleanup call" (issue #5068 acceptance criterion; PR description "Findings fixed" finding 5: "The twin's step 2 now says the later sweep leaves the denied id out... and the Arming-the-wait step 0 sweep now says to leave out ids denied earlier"). The PR description's review-round-2 reply claims "Fixed in 52897d3: implement-plan-claude.md:20, root and twin" but the root command was not actually fixed.
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md lines 20 and 204, plus tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py to assert the root command matches the twin's corrected wording.
  Evidence of absence: At .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:20, the final clause still reads "a later sweep (Arming the wait, step 0) removes what it would have" — the contradictory wording the twin no longer carries. At line 204, the root command still says "Run the stale Routine sweep (CLAUDE.md §26.G)." with no exclusion cue, unlike the twin which says "leaving out every trigger id whose `delete_trigger` was denied earlier in this session". The test `test_step_2_sweep_is_skipped_after_a_denied_delete` at tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:385 only checks `twin_text`, not the root command, so it passes while the root remains broken. The PR description acknowledges the root will change in the "tenth [claude-twin-sync]" but that sync has not happened yet, so the current state has the root command with the runtime defect. The issue's acceptance criterion is not fully met because sessions following the root command will retry a denied cleanup call.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
